# Results — Study 502 (Betting-Against-Correlation) on a real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: monthly
Betting-Against-Correlation book — rank a large-cap survivor cross-section by trailing
252-day **correlation-to-market**, long the low-correlation half, short the
**beta-neutralised** high-correlation half, one execution lag (enter the close one trading day
after the signal). Measured vs SPY. As-of **2026-06-26**. Inputs fingerprint `3f75d60c45d8`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `WEAK` · Tradability `FRAGILE` · "Is it correlation, not vol?" `CONFIRMED`

Asness, Frazzini, Gormsen & Pedersen (2020) decompose Betting-Against-Beta into a
correlation slice (BAC) and a volatility slice (BAV), and argue the **correlation** slice
carries the premium. On a 48-name large-cap survivor panel, 2013–2025 (150 months), the BAC
book earns **+3.75%/yr gross** at HAC *t* = **+1.54**, **+3.36%/yr net** of 5 bps/leg + 50 bps
borrow (*t* +1.39) — short of the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar, with a block-bootstrap 95% CI on the
annual mean of **[−1.0%, +8.5%]** that straddles zero. So `WEAK` on the signal axis. But the
**decomposition vindicates the paper's central claim**: on the *same* panel, sorting on
**correlation** earns +3.75%/yr while sorting on **beta** (BAB) earns −0.67%/yr and on
**volatility** (BAV) earns −0.87%/yr — the premium lives in the correlation component, exactly
as AFGP predict (`CONFIRMED`). And the effect is structurally real even where it is statistically
thin: a label-shuffle placebo puts the real mean in the **right tail, p = 0.04**.

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 3424 days × 48 tickers | `3f75d60c45d8` |
| SPY (market proxy) | 4023 days | `0324b1d986de` |
| Common price window | 2012-05-18 — 2025-12-30 | — |
| BAC book | 150 months (2013-06 — 2025-11) | — |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True). Universe: 48 large-cap
names spanning mega-cap tech (high correlation to a tech-heavy SPY), financials/cyclicals,
defensives/staples/health, utilities and energy/commodity names (the lowest correlation).
Risk-free rate = 3%/yr constant (no FRED). One execution lag (enter close one day after signal).

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** every name still trades in 2026. The high-correlation
short leg is therefore missing the failed names a real BAC short would have caught, and the
low-correlation long leg is a basket of survivors. All positive results are **upper-bound**
estimates. *Opt-in guard:* re-run `fetch_panel` against a point-in-time membership list to
restore the delisted names — the desk does not own one, so this study names the bias and treats
the number as a ceiling.

## The honest test — BAC book construction

Trailing 252-day correlation-to-market and beta estimated for each name vs SPY. Each month,
names are split at the **median correlation**: the long leg is the low-correlation half, the
short leg the high-correlation half (equal weight within a leg). The short leg is scaled by
`avg_beta_long / avg_beta_short` so the book's ex-ante market beta ≈ 0 — without this the "edge"
would just be a hidden short of high-beta exposure (the conflation AFGP warn against, and the
line separating this from [238 Betting-Against-Beta](../../238-betting-against-beta/)).

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 150 (2013-06 — 2025-11) |
| Gross mean (annualised) | **+3.75%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 9.10%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | +0.412 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+1.543** |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 56.7% |
| Max drawdown | −20.9% |
| Block-bootstrap 95% CI (ann mean) | **[−1.0%, +8.5%]** |
| Net mean (5 bps/leg + 50 bps borrow) | **+3.36%/yr** (*t* +1.385) |

- The BAC book earns **+3.75%/yr** at HAC *t* = **+1.543** — below the inference bar of
  |*t*| ≥ 2. The bootstrap CI straddles zero. On this 13-year large-cap survivor panel the
  correlation premium is **positive but not statistically certifiable**.
- The sort separates cleanly: the long leg averages correlation **0.41**, the short leg **0.67**;
  after neutralisation the long-leg beta is **0.73** and the short-leg beta **1.18** (avg short
  weight 0.64).
- Both legs are *up* in raw terms (long +15.2%/yr, short +16.7%/yr, SPY +13.0%/yr): the book's
  edge is the spread, not either leg in isolation.

## Is it correlation, not volatility? — the AFGP decomposition

The *same* engine, same panel, same neutralisation — only the **sort variable** changes:

| Sort variable | Mean (ann) | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Correlation (BAC)** | **+3.75%/yr** | **+0.412** | **+1.543** |
| Beta (BAB) | −0.67%/yr | −0.071 | −0.288 |
| Volatility (BAV) | −0.87%/yr | −0.096 | −0.384 |

This is the study's headline finding. On this panel the premium is **carried entirely by the
correlation slice**: sorting on beta or on volatility earns *nothing* (indeed slightly negative),
while sorting on correlation earns the +3.75%/yr. That is precisely the AFGP (2020) claim — the
BAB premium is a correlation effect, not a volatility effect. The 3rd-axis question
*"is it correlation, not vol?"* is **`CONFIRMED`**, even though the magnitude is too thin to clear
*t* = 2 on a survivor basket.

## Robustness — label-shuffle placebo

The correlation ranks are permuted across names before forming the legs (signal destroyed; panel,
neutralisation, costs and lag identical). Over **200 shuffles**:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Real mean / month | +0.313% |
| Placebo mean / month | +0.005% (± 0.164%) |
| One-sided p-value | **0.040** |

The real BAC mean sits in the **right tail** of the shuffled-null distribution (p = 0.04): the
correlation labels are doing real work — the spread is *not* an artefact of the construction. So
the signal is structurally real even though, on 150 months, it does not clear the HAC *t* = 2 bar.

## Synthetic positive control (seed-robust, 20 seeds/point)

A deterministic synthetic panel plants a correlation-keyed premium of increasing strength; the
beta-neutral book's HAC *t* is averaged over 20 independent seeds per point (no single lucky RNG
draw can manufacture the result — the house rule for any synthetic-dependent claim):

| Planted premium | Mean HAC *t* (± sd) |
|---|---|
| 0.0%/yr (null) | +0.30 (± 0.95) |
| 2.0%/yr | +0.50 (± 0.95) |
| 4.0%/yr | +0.69 (± 0.95) |
| 6.0%/yr | +0.89 (± 0.95) |
| 8.0%/yr | +1.08 (± 0.94) |
| 10.0%/yr | +1.28 (± 0.94) |

The *t* sits at ~0 at the null and climbs monotonically with the planted premium — a faithful
detector. (The slope is gentle because a 48-name / ~120-month panel is genuinely
low-powered; the control is a faithful-engine check, **not** evidence for the real-tape stamp.)

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Gross +3.75%/yr at HAC *t* = +1.543, net +3.36%/yr at *t* = +1.385 — both
  below |*t*| ≥ 2; the bootstrap CI [−1.0%, +8.5%] straddles zero. The label-shuffle placebo
  (p = 0.04) and the AFGP (2020) literature give the effect real prior support, so it is WEAK
  rather than NONE — but on 150 months of large-cap survivors it does not independently clear
  the bar.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Sharpe +0.41, max drawdown −20.9%; the book needs a short leg
  (borrow charged) and lives or dies on dispersion (the 2020 and 2023 correlation-spike years
  are brutal: −11.5% and −16.2%). Net of realistic costs the +3.4%/yr survives but is thin and
  uncertain.
- **Is it correlation, not vol? — CONFIRMED.** On this panel the correlation sort earns
  +3.75%/yr while the beta and volatility sorts earn nothing — the premium really does live in
  the correlation component, exactly as AFGP predict. The mechanism is real; the tradable
  magnitude on a survivor basket is not certifiable.
